entities.name: 'artificial general intelligence' / 'AGI'
terms: general artificial intelligence (searched, not the term)
entities.criterion: A passage uses the words 'artificial general intelligence' (or the abbreviation 'AGI' for them) as a name for machine intelligence of general, broadly human-level or greater scope; 'general intelligence' alone, 'strong AI' and 'general artificial intelligence' do not meet it.

search.venues: Crossref REST API (query.bibliographic, publication dates up to 1997-12-31, 1,000 top-ranked records per query screened for the exact phrase in titles and deposited abstracts); Semantic Scholar bulk search (exact phrase, year ≤ 1997, titles and abstracts); Europe PMC (exact phrase, 1900–1997, titles, abstracts and full texts it indexes); the full texts retrieved for this group (Good 1965, the Dartmouth facsimile pages read as images, Vinge 1993, Gubrud 1997, Bostrom 1997/1998 with postscripts, Legg and Hutter 2007, McCarthy's two pages); SL4 mailing-list subject indexes, every month from 2000-02 to 2002-06 (subject lines only); citation following from Goertzel's 2011 account. arXiv API (exact phrase in all fields, ascending by submission date): earliest record 2003-02-10 (Schmidhuber, 'The New AI: General & Sound & Relevant for Physics'), none before 1998 (arXiv holds little before the 1990s).
search.years: Indexes: everything they hold up to 1997-12-31. SL4: 2000-02 to 2002-06. Retrieved texts: 1955–2011.
search.methods: Exact-phrase filters on index records (titles and abstracts only, not full text, except Europe PMC's open full texts); full-text grep of retrieved texts for 'artificial general intelligence', 'general intelligence' and '\bAGI\b'; subject-line grep of SL4 indexes; following Goertzel's 2011 pointer to Gubrud 1997.
search.gaps: No full-text search of books, magazines, conference proceedings or Usenet before 1997 was possible: Google Books (API daily quota exhausted), the Internet Archive's full-text scholar search (rate-limited, 429) and OpenAlex (rate-limited) did not answer on 2026-10-29, and Usenet archives (Google Groups) are not retrievable here. Index records before 1997 rarely carry abstracts, so a use in a body text would not be found. Crossref and Semantic Scholar returned no record with the phrase before 1998; Semantic Scholar returned four records for 'general artificial intelligence' (1983–1991) without abstracts, not opened and not the term. Extropians list archives 1996–2001 and SL4 message bodies were not searched. The 2007 Springer volume and Goertzel's 2014 survey were not retrieved.
search.failures: Google Books API (quota exceeded); scholar.archive.org (429); OpenAlex API (rate limit); web.archive.org availability and CDX services (429 and connection reset), so no capture address is recorded for the Foresight pages; sciendo.com and degruyter.com for Goertzel 2014 (403 and 202 challenge); link.springer.com (client challenge); agi-conf.org (403 challenge); dblp.org (Anubis challenge); vetta.org (TLS chain not verifiable over https; bot check 401 over http). Retried later in the session: the Archive availability service (429), scholar.archive.org (rate-limit page) and OpenAlex (daily budget exhausted) still did not answer.

corrections.reason: Same-family audit: Gubrud (1997) is read only in the Foresight Archives’ current, undated copy; under the editorial policy a text known only from an undated later copy cannot be earliest located. A 1997–1998 capture of http://www.foresight.org/Conferences/MNT05/Papers/Gubrud/ (or the conference’s printed proceedings) would decide the role. Goertzel (2011) separately reports a 1997 article by Gubrud.

entities.note: Earliest located: Gubrud's 1997 conference paper. The abbreviation 'AGI' is earliest located in the texts searched in Goertzel's SL4 message of 2002-05-19; this is a note, not a second headline, because the concept takes the full term and its abbreviation together. Goertzel's 2011 account attributes the suggestion of the term for the 2007 book title to Shane Legg and reports Gubrud's earlier use; both are attributed statements.

entities.name: 'superintelligence'
terms: superintelligent (adjective; recorded in the search only)
entities.criterion: A passage uses the noun 'superintelligence' (or 'super-intelligence') for an intellect, machine or mind that greatly exceeds human intelligence, in the context of artificial or post-human minds; a use for exceptionally gifted humans, aliens or a deity is other-sense.

search.venues: Crossref REST API (queries 'superintelligence', 'super-intelligence' and 'superintelligent', publication dates up to 1997-12-31, top 1,000 records screened for the strings in titles and abstracts); Semantic Scholar bulk search (exact 'superintelligence', year ≤ 1997); Europe PMC (the three strings, 1900–1997); full texts retrieved for this group (Good 1965, Vinge 1993, the Extropians messages of 1996-08-30, 1996-09-03 (two) and 1996-11-19 in the dataset, Bostrom 1997/1998). arXiv API (all fields): earliest record 2014-05-14.
search.methods: String filters on index titles and abstracts; full-text grep of retrieved texts for 'super-?intellig'; comparison with the dataset's earliest quoted use (Yudkowsky, 'Staring into the Singularity', 1996-11-18 wording attested in a 2000 capture).
search.gaps: Index hits not retrieved: 'Genes for super-intelligence?' (Journal of Medical Genetics, 1981 and 1982 correspondence; doi 10.1136/jmg.18.6.410 and others; human sense on its face; jmg.bmj.com and pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov answered 403 or a challenge); 'Are all aliens super-intelligent?' (Science and Public Policy, 1987; adjective, aliens); 'Clive Sinclair: towards the superintelligent machine' (Computer Bulletin / ITNOW 32(8), 1990, doi 10.1093/combul/32.8.12; adjective, machine sense on its face; academic.oup.com 403); a 1982 Krankenpflege Journal item '[Superintelligent--but unrecognized]' (adjective, human sense on its face, not opened); Europe PMC full-text hits of 1908–1947 (BMJ 1921, Eugenics Review 1922 and others) whose scans were not served (challenge). Semantic Scholar matched two records (1976, 1994) without visible text; not verified. Books (for example Moravec 1988) and Usenet were not searched; Google Books and the Internet Archive full-text search did not answer. 'Superintelligent' (adjective) is outside the criterion and is listed here only.
search.failures: jmg.bmj.com (403); academic.oup.com (403); pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov PDF of BMJ 1921 (challenge); Google Books API (quota); scholar.archive.org (429); OpenAlex (rate limit).

openQuestions.question: Should Gubrud 1997 hold the 'AGI' headline while its wording is read only from the Foresight Archives' current copy, with no capture checked?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes, provisionally: the copy is the organiser's archive of the 1997 conference, the abstract page ties it to that conference, and Goertzel's 2011 account independently reports a 1997 use. Before admission, look up a 1997–1998 capture of www.foresight.org/Conferences/MNT05/Papers/Gubrud/index.html (the cross-family checker may reach the Archive) and record it as the attested date.

openQuestions.question: Is a full-text search before 1997 (Google Books, the Internet Archive's texts, Usenet) needed before calling Gubrud the earliest located?
openQuestions.recommended: Run it in the cross-family check if any of those services answers; until then the search block states that body texts before 1997 were not searched, and the headline is 'earliest located' only.

openQuestions.question: Which publication year should the Goertzel–Pennachin volume carry: 2007 (publisher metadata) or 2005 (Goertzel's post, and one of Legg and Hutter's references)?
openQuestions.recommended: Carry 2007 as the publication date and keep 2005 as a claimed date with both sources side by side; do not resolve until the book's imprint page is read.

openQuestions.question: Should the 1990 Computer Bulletin item 'Clive Sinclair: towards the superintelligent machine' be read before admission, since its adjective form predates Vinge's noun?
openQuestions.recommended: Yes if a copy can be reached; it does not change the 'superintelligence' headline (the criterion takes the noun), but it belongs in the term's search note as the earliest machine-sense adjective found by index.

openQuestions.question: Does the Legg–Hutter definition of intelligence belong under th-term-agi?
openQuestions.recommended: Keep it only if the maintainer wants the term's page to carry the persons' own definitional work; otherwise drop th-def-intelligence-legg-hutter-2007, since the paper does not define 'artificial general intelligence'.
